title: The Truth of God's Testimonies
english: The wise one announced the law and the prophets, saying, 'The revelation of your words makes me understand'; but he did not see these things in a prophetic spirit, for whoever possesses their understanding desired that which was to be revealed before the coming of Christ.

He is worthy to see and learn the shining forth of the Savior this time, saying to the Savior about it, 'Let your face shine, so that whoever seeing you may see you' (Ps 118:135). For he himself says about himself, 'He who has seen me has seen the Father' (John 14:9). For since this exists, he says, it will be possible for me to learn your ordinances. And to learn that is to walk in them, not according to the flesh but according to grace.

Therefore your judgment is straight, because you are just, judging all those who received your judgments straight according to the canons of righteousness, since I commanded truth and righteousness intensely (Ps 118:137). For I commanded your divine writings to men, not only the new ones but also the old ones, being just according to ethics and truth, that is, being precise according to the view of things according to which I commanded us to make judgments, so that we might judge the great and the small, judging a just judgment intensely, they are truth and righteousness (Ps 118:138).

Therefore that word so ignited is made to him intensely loved by something, making him a servant of God burning in the spirit (Ps 118:140). Such a person, when the Scriptures are made clear by Jesus, is amazed in heart, as saying according to the [Road to] Emmaus, 'Did not our heart burn within us when he opened the Scriptures to us?' (Luke 24:32).

For he is unswerving and unchangeable, never having or not having righteousness, being the source and generator of it (Ps 118:142); and his word is truth, being truth to those hearing for all eternity, not being such a human word; for the word of human wisdom, to become in glory...

Being false, after the truth has been revealed, he will be convicted of being false (Ps 118:144). I have given you testimonies not for a short time, but they prove to be useful righteousness for eternity, justifying the one who possesses them by drawing near to them.

First, in an unseasonable time—that is, what is called night in this present age, often called day as if for the coming age, according to 'The night has passed, and the day is near' (Ps 118:147)—but the perceptive powers of his eyes, acting as eyes, reach forward toward the righteousness coming from the rising of the sun. Therefore, having been enlightened and finding himself in the light, he meditates on the commandments of God, which cause him to fly to be lifted up and to approach the true light nakedly, so that he may find himself no longer in an unseasonable time, but in a peak and midday light.

Another scripture says: 'And all your ways are truth' (Ps 118:151), clearly meaning those paths leading to Him; for the end of all these ways is He who said, 'I am the way, and the truth, and the life' (John 14:6). He who has reached the goal of these ways is in truth, having both it and its Father within himself. And since He also approaches the sinners in another way, He is near to them; and all His ways are truth, for as one travels them, He performs the examination and judgment of their affairs.

The testimonies were established by God so that no one would be able to shake or overturn them; for your word is wisdom, and your Son is their foundation. Therefore, presenting their unassailable and unshakeable nature, He says, 'My words will never pass away, even if heaven and earth pass away' (Matt 24:35).
Often, when 'the beginning' is taken in a certain sense, we say the beginning is the truth of the words of God, as that which is first. For to make it known...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
